newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland seeks VAT cut on imported citrus fruit.
newsitem.headline: Poland seeks VAT cut on imported citrus fruit.

text.p: Poland seeks to lower its value-added tax on imported citrus fruits to seven from 22 percent from the beginning of 1998, the secretary of the government's European Integration Committee said on Friday.
"We want to lower the VAT rate on citrus fruits from the beginning of next year," PAP news agency quoted Danuta Hubner as telling a news conference late on Friday.
The proposal must be approved by the cabinet at its meeting on Tuesday.
On Thursday Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told Reuters in an interview that scrapping the 22-percent VAT would cost the budget some 200 million zlotys ($65 million) in lost revenues.

Hubner on Friday said Poland's policy change would have a postive impact at next week's European Union-Poland Association Council meeting, during which Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati will meet his EU counterparts.
She said she hoped there would now be an opening of EU markets to Polish farm products, which would help improve Poland's negative trade balance with EU countries.
"The meeting will be a good one because it has been possible to solve many issues. The issue of assembly of Daewoo cars has also ended happily," PAP quoted Hubner as saying, giving no other details.

The EU has objected to a deal by which Poland has allowed South Korean carmaker Daewoo Motor Co to import tens of thousands of car kits a year duty-free as part of its purchase last year of the FSO car plant in Warsaw.
